docs.title: Hi, I'm Guglielmo Grillo aka NerusSkyhigh.
About me
docs.text: Hi, I'm Guglielmo Grillo, but you will most likely find me online as NerusSkyhigh. I am a PhD student in Physics at the University of Trento (Statistical and Biological Physics group) with a strong passion for computer science. This passion led me to choose a computational path both for my curricular and extracurricular classes during my bachelor's and Master's degrees and to work on personal projects in my free time. I’m also one of the founding members of Progetto Apollo, a scientific divulgation group operating at the University of Trento in collaboration with Arditodesìo. Since 2019 I’ve been a tutor for the University of Trento. My hobbies include video games, DMing d&d campaigns and parkour.

docs.title: Slides and Talk
docs.text:
• Do not put slide number in your presentation. But put some id to have them referenced later
    • Maybe the slide number is ok. The total amount is NOT.

  • Put title, name, date, and event at the bottom of every page

  • Backup slides (think how many)

  • Images can be used as page index. Assume to have three sections represented by three images. You can put at the beginning of each section the images with different transparency and at the bottom of each slide a smaller version of the outline. Slide1: [img1, alpha=1] -> [img2, alpha=0.5] -> [img3, alpha=0.5] Slide2: [img1, alpha=0.5] -> [img2, alpha=1] -> [img3, alpha=0.5] Slide3: [img1, alpha=0.5] -> [img2, alpha=0.5] -> [img3, alpha=1]

  • Don't put equations unless you have to. Ideally have at most one equation (or system of equations) per slide.

  • The presentation is about you, not the slides. Ideally, the slides should provide all the topic, but it is you that will make them understandable/give insight on the content. e.g. If the slide contains the formula \(P_{ij}=C \max\left\{ P_i, P_j \right\}\) a straightforward deduction is that \(P_{ij} = P_{ji}\). Don't write it. Say it!. You are there to communicate insight, not to read formula. The formula can be found in the paper. At the same time, if you write the deduction, you are going to “lose value” as a speaker and people will start reading the slides instead of listening to you, thus losing focus.

  • Introduce EVERY concept with an elevator pitch. Then dig deeper into the topic.

  • General introduction with the importance / connections of your work

  • Overview: outline what happens in each section
  • Reference of images in didascaly
  • Put things in the slide but jump over it saying "we can come back to this later if you want"

  • Put highlights AFTER empty slides. If the slide already presents an highlight it looks ugly and doesn't highlight anything.

  • It is also interesting the idea to change color to part of an equation to highlight the interesting term (Degio's idea)

  • If the presentation is particularly long, have in-between brief summaries to recap the main concepts of each part.

  • Aggiungere il logo dell'università ed eventuali enti associati

  • Reference

  • Se possibile aggiugnere animazioni per spiegare fenomeni

[!warning] Le slides servono per spiegare, non sono un sostituto alla tesi/note

  • Final slides can be:

    • bibliography
    • a photo of the group you're in
    • personal info so that the audience can follow up

  • Una slide un concetto

  • Attenzione al lessico ed il livello di tecnicismi. Adattalo all'audience! (spiega come spiegheresti a tua nonna. Aiuta anche a fare ordine nelle tue idee)

  • Evita:

    • Inglesismi (a meno di pubblico giovane e da intrattenere (?) )
    • Acronimi non standard e non chiari

  • Nell'introduzione puoi quantificare per dare un'idea della grandezza del problema. Usare numeri aiuta a far sembrare la presentazione migliore.

  • Ovviamente, prepararsi e ripetere permette di non perdere il filo ed andare avanti Divide presentation into three main area / topics.

Also, when using bold type, remember that people will read those word first. If you can, try have them convey a message on its own.

Instead of generic titles like "The Model" or "Results" try to have meaningful short sentences that describe the key point or summarize the meaning of the slide.

A good alternative for "thank for your attention" is to go back to the conclusions so that people will have an outline to focus onto.

  • try to match room light, dark background is good in darker rooms and vice-versa.

  • A good way to have yourself found is to write your name followed by your institution. Google will do the rest.

  • Point only part of the equations. Those who don't know the equation won't understand it during your talk (unless it is YOUR equation). Just point out the important terms and explain why they are important.

docs.title: During your talk
docs.text:
• Non distribuire omogeneamente gli sguardi. Fai un sampling in base all'importanza del pubblico senza tralasciare nessuno.
  • Usa la posizione sul palco per demarcare bene il passaggio fra i vari concetti e punti logici.
  • Non fare random walk, cercare di muoversi il minimo possibile e, se non diversamente necessario, cercare di mantenere una postura neutrale
  • "abbraccia" con lo sguardo tutto il pubblico. In questo modo si sentiranno più partecipi
  • Non appoggiarti al muro
  • Se per qualche motivo il palco ha zone d'ombra stacci lontano
  • Siccome ti presentano, invece di presentarti tu usa il momento per ringraziare gli organizzatori
  • Nel caso di diretta su zoom, fai attenzione che non ci siano icone, widget, cazziemazzi vari in mezzo allo schermo. Rischiano di oscurare cose importanti.
  • Spiega le sigle, anche se sono biologiche.
  • Evita la slide "Thank you" e, se proprio devi, torna alle conclusioni durante le domande.

docs.title: Classroom Tutor
docs.text: In the in-class courses, my task as a tutor was to prepare ad-hoc exercises beforehand and then follow the students in their reasoning by providing hints and guidance toward the solution. In the laboratory courses, our job was to explain the lab experiences to the students and assist them in the data collection and analysis ensuring that they understood the underlying reasoning and scientific approach.

docs.text:
Institution: University of Trento (Italy)

I was assigned to the following courses:

  • Sep 2022-Dec 2022: Introductory Physics Laboratory (DII), Mathematical Basis for Cognitive Sciences (CIMEC), Mathematics and Statistics I (CIBIO);
  • Mar 2022-June 2022: Laboratory of Physics I with Matlab (DF), Introductory Physics Laboratory (DICAM);

The underlined courses represent the courses for which I was the only tutor. In all other courses, I was part of a team of 2 to 4 tutors.

docs.title: Storyteller / Science Communicator
docs.text: I'm one of the founding members of Progetto Apollo, a scientific divulgation group operating at the University of Trento in collaboration with Arditodesìo. Some of our activities include research on a key topic or an interview with a Professor at the University of Trento to write narratives with the principles of storytelling.

docs.title: Additional Info
docs.text:
Institution: Arditodesìo / University of Trento (Italy) Date: 2017-2022

The plays were then performed in the course of various editions of Teatro della Meraviglia, EIT RAW Materials 2021, CO.SCIENZA Festival 2019, Focus Days 2019 and Fisicittà 2017. In 2022 we partnered with Caltech for the event “La Terra fatta dagli umani” (Earth made by humans) about the beginning of the Anthropocene. The resulting performances were presented both in Trento and at Caltech.

docs.title: PhD in  Physics
docs.text: Scholarship: Combining physics, biology and machine learning to understand genome organization in cancer cells Group: Statistical and Biological Physics Group Supervisor: prof. L. Tubiana

docs.title: Master's Degree in Physics
docs.text:
Path: Statistical Biophysics with a focus on computational methods Final Grade: 110/110

Thesis: Computational Models Of Astrocyte-Neuron Dynamics To Explain The Formation Of Working Memory Supervisor: prof. L. Tubiana

The thesis aimed to explore the characteristics of various effective models for neurons with the purpose of finding an effective representation compatible with a description of memory formation via the coupling between neurons and astrocytes. All the models were implemented in Python from scratch.

CyberChallenge.IT is a course designed to provide the methodological and practical basis to analyze vulnerabilities and possible attacks and identify the most suitable solutions to prevent them.

docs.title: Bachelor's Degree in Physics
docs.text:
Thesis: Emergent features: from renormalization group to artificial intelligence Supervisor: prof. R. Potestio

The thesis focussed on a possible explanation behind the efficiency of machine learning models. In particular, the link between Restricted Boltzmann Machines applied to the Ising Model and a renormalization procedure was examined.

After graduating, I enrolled in the course "Introduction to Data Science for Physicists" as a listener (March-June 2020).
